title: Emergency delivery and third stage
stem: ED delivery room. A woman at 39 weeks in her second pregnancy is pushing, with the head crowning. The obstetric team is 15 minutes away. Conduct the delivery and the third stage on the manikin.

phases.title: Prepare
phases.goal: Two teams, the pack, warmth, and oxytocin drawn up.

phases.title: Deliver the baby
phases.goal: A controlled delivery of the head, the cord, the shoulders.

review.text: Routine oxytocic. Your notes choose Syntometrine. NICE recommends oxytocin 10 IU IM for the third stage: fewer side effects (vomiting, hypertension). Your point that Syntometrine is contraindicated in pre-eclampsia stands.

notes:
Checked against NICE NG235 (Intrapartum care, 2023, which carries on the CG190 recommendations), NICE QS105 statement 6 (delayed cord clamping) and RCOG guidance.

The birth (NICE): 'hands on' (guarding the perineum and flexing the head) or 'hands poised' may be used; the station teaches hands on. No routine episiotomy. As the head crowns she pants rather than pushes, so it is born slowly between contractions. Feel for a nuchal cord: slip a loose loop over the head; a tight one, 'somersault' delivery; clamping and cutting before the birth is a last resort. Wait for restitution (the head turns to face a thigh: left occipito-anterior turns to her right). With the next contraction, gentle downward axial traction for the anterior shoulder, then upward for the posterior; never hard or lateral traction (brachial plexus). Onto the mother's abdomen skin to skin, the time of birth noted, dried, the wet towel swapped for a dry one and a hat, breathing, tone and colour checked. Routine suctioning is not recommended.

Third stage (NICE): active management is a uterotonic, deferred clamping and cutting of the cord, and controlled cord traction after signs of separation. Oxytocin 10 IU IM after the birth of the baby and before the cord is clamped and cut (palpate first to exclude a second twin). Do not clamp the cord earlier than 1 minute after the birth unless there is concern about cord integrity or a heart rate below 60/min that is not getting faster (QS105); clamp before 5 minutes to perform controlled cord traction. Signs of separation: a gush of blood, cord lengthening, the fundus rising and becoming firm and globular. Traction with the other hand guarding the uterus above the pubis (prevents inversion); twist the membranes out. Check the placenta and membranes are complete and the cord has three vessels; rub up the fundus; inspect for tears; measure the blood loss (weighing pads, the jug): a visual estimate underestimates it. Prolonged third stage: not completed within 30 minutes with active management, or 60 minutes with physiological management. Your notes' 30 minutes is correct for active management.

Your notes choose Syntometrine for routine use; NICE recommends oxytocin 10 IU IM (fewer side effects: vomiting, hypertension). Syntometrine is contraindicated in pre-eclampsia, as your notes say.

Changed from the earlier version: cord clamping moved from the birth into the third stage, after the oxytocin, as NICE orders it. The bench has no wrong-move buttons (no clamp-and-cut-now, no routine suction, no blood-loss guess): mistakes come from doing a real action badly (pushing through crowning, pulling hard, pulling before separation, cutting outside the clamps).

Perfect script checked against NICE NG235 intrapartum care, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme.

script.say: Call obstetrics and neonatology; one team for mother, one for baby. PPE; sterile delivery pack with two clamps and scissors. Warm towels, hat, resuscitaire on.
Oxytocin 10 IU drawn up for the third stage.

Pad guarding the perineum, my palm on the head to keep it flexed; as it crowns, 'pant, don't push'. Feel for a cord: a loose loop slips over the head. Wait for restitution. With the next contraction, gentle downward axial traction for the anterior shoulder, then upward for the posterior. Onto mum's tummy skin to skin; time of birth; dry her, dry towel and hat; check breathing, tone and colour.

Feel the abdomen: no second twin; oxytocin 10 IU IM. After at least 60 seconds, clamp and cut the cord. Wait for separation: a gush of blood, the cord lengthening, the fundus rising. Controlled cord traction with my other hand guarding the uterus above the pubis; twist the membranes out. Check the placenta, membranes and three cord vessels; the fundus firm; tears; measured blood loss.
